title: Infostealers
overview: Look for unexpected reads of a browser credential-store category by a process without established trust.
prerequisites: Know the basics of Windows auditing and how to review authorization context.

attack.name: Credentials from Web Browsers
attack.rationale: The behavior in this lesson corresponds to this technique; the fixture models a defensive observation.

hypothesis: An unapproved non-browser reader accessing credential storage should be correlated with process provenance and account risk.
evidence: Compare credential-store classification, actor image, trust and related process or network observations.
false_positive: A sanctioned migration or endpoint backup could read profile storage.
tuning: Tune by verified publisher and reviewed operation. Keep exceptions distinct from browser session-store access.
response: Isolate an affected endpoint if corroborated, identify exposed accounts and rotate credentials through approved policy.
prevention: Apply endpoint hardening, managed browser policy and monitored credential-store access.
validation: Baseline and noisy fixture produce no alerts. The positive fixture produces an alert with linked evidence.
limitations: No secret value or profile database is present. The access record does not show successful credential decryption.

questions.explanation: Credential-store access and session-cookie access are different observations.

options: Related process, endpoint and account events
questions.explanation: Additional telemetry helps determine whether access led to credential use.
